title: The zero set of a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals on an affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals (a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal O_X$ which is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]). For $x\in X$ regard the stalk $\mathcal K_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] as an ideal of the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ (the map $\mathcal K_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ induced by the inclusion is injective, stalks being filtered colimits), and put $V(\mathcal K)=\{x\in X:\mathcal K_x\neq\mathcal O_{X,x}\}$. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, and identify $U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] by the canonical open immersion $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ with image $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], the point $x\in U$ corresponding to the prime $\mathfrak p_x\subset A$. Then for $x\in U$: $\mathcal K_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ if and only if $\mathcal K(U)\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$. That is, $V(\mathcal K)\cap U=V(\mathcal K(U))=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A:\mathcal K(U)\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$; consequently $V(\mathcal K)$ is a closed subset of $X$, and it is the underlying set of the closed subscheme of $X$ cut out by $\mathcal K$: for every closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is $\mathcal K$ (one exists [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme]), $i(Z)=V(\mathcal K)$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (transport to $\operatorname{Spec}A$).* Let $\iota=\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ be the open immersion with image $U$ and $\iota(\mathfrak p_x)=x$ for $x\in U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. Restrict along $\iota$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]: $\mathcal K'=\mathcal K|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ has $\mathcal K'(V)=\mathcal K(\iota(V))$, and $\mathcal O_X|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ has $\mathcal O_X(\iota(V))\cong\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}(V)$ by $\iota^\sharp$, so $\mathcal O_X|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\cong\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ and the restriction $j'$ of the inclusion $j:\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_X$ makes $\mathcal K'$ a sub-$\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$-module of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ (each $j'_V=j_{\iota(V)}$ is an inclusion). By part (2) of that lemma $\mathcal K'$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Its global sections are $\mathcal K'(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\mathcal K(U)$, an ideal $I$ of $A=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] under the identification $\iota^\sharp:\mathcal O_X(U)\cong A$ of the statement. Stalks: for $x=\iota(\mathfrak p)$, the open neighbourhoods $\iota(V)$ ($V\ni\mathfrak p$ open) of $x$ are cofinal among all open neighbourhoods $W$ of $x$ ($W\supseteq W\cap U=\iota(\iota^{-1}W)$), so the colimits defining the stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] agree: $\mathcal K_x=\mathcal K'_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathfrak p}$ (by $\iota^\sharp$ on germs), and $j_x$ corresponds to $j'_{\mathfrak p}$. So it suffices to prove: for $\mathcal K'\subseteq\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals with $\mathcal K'(\operatorname{Spec}A)=I$ and a prime $\mathfrak p$, $j'_{\mathfrak p}(\mathcal K'_{\mathfrak p})=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathfrak p}$ iff $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Below write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\mathcal K$ for $\mathcal K'$ and $j$ for $j'$.

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\mathcal K_{\mathfrak p}$ is an ideal of $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$).* $j_V$ is injective for every open $V$, so the $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$-linear stalk map $j_{\mathfrak p}:\mathcal K_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$ is injective [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (1), and its image is an ideal of the ring $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$ (an $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$-submodule of $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$, stalk maps being $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]); this is the identification of $\mathcal K_x$ with an ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ made in the statement.

proof.text: *Step 3 (the image of $j_{\mathfrak p}$ is $I\,\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$).* Let $\rho:A\to\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$, $a\mapsto a_{\mathfrak p}$, be the germ map; it is a localization of $A$ at $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (1). Let $\widetilde I$ and $\tau_Y:I\to\widetilde I(Y)$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Since $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent (Step 1), the counit $\varepsilon:\widetilde{\Gamma(Y,\mathcal K)}=\widetilde I\to\mathcal K$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3); as it corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_I$ under $\alpha\mapsto\alpha_Y\circ\tau_Y$ (part (1)), $\varepsilon_Y(\tau_Y(a))=a\in\mathcal K(Y)=I$ for $a\in I$. Its stalk $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak p}:\widetilde I_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal K_{\mathfrak p}$ is an $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$-linear bijection (the stalk of the inverse is inverse to it, stalks being functorial [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], $\lambda_I:I\to\widetilde I_{\mathfrak p}$, $a\mapsto\tau_Y(a)_{\mathfrak p}$, is a localization of $I$ at $S$, $\widetilde I_{\mathfrak p}$ being an $A$-module through $\rho$; by its property (b) every element of $\widetilde I_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\rho(s)^{-1}\lambda_I(a)$ with $a\in I$, $s\in S$. Now $j_{\mathfrak p}(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_I(a)))=j_{\mathfrak p}(\varepsilon_Y(\tau_Y(a))_{\mathfrak p})=(j_Y(a))_{\mathfrak p}=\rho(a)$, since $j_Y$ is the inclusion $I\subseteq A$. As $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective and $j_{\mathfrak p}\circ\varepsilon_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}$-linear, $j_{\mathfrak p}(\mathcal K_{\mathfrak p})=\{\rho(s)^{-1}\rho(a):a\in I,\ s\in S\}$.

proof.text: *Step 5 ($V(\mathcal K)=i(Z)$, closed).* Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)=\mathcal K$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; one exists by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-image-zero-locus], $i(Z)$ is closed in $X$ and for every affine open $U$ of $X$, $i(Z)\cap U=\{x\in U:\mathcal K(U)\subseteq\mathfrak p_x\}$, with $\mathfrak p_x$ defined through the same open immersion $\iota_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]; by Step 4 this is $V(\mathcal K)\cap U$. Every point of the scheme $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood [def-pc-scheme], so the affine opens cover $X$ and $V(\mathcal K)=\bigcup_U V(\mathcal K)\cap U=\bigcup_U i(Z)\cap U=i(Z)$, a closed subset of $X$.
